newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs demand equal rights for gay couples.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs demand equal rights for gay couples.

text.p: The European Parliament said on Thursday the European Union institutions must ban discrimination against their own staff on the basis of sexual orientation or age.

Homosexual EU civil servants involved in a permanent relationship should be treated on the same footing as married heterosexual officials, thus giving them the same financial and social entitlements, Euro-MPs said in a report.
The report also demands that the European Commission, the Council of Ministers and the parliament abolish a rule preventing the hiring of civil servants who are over 35 at the time they apply.

The report, adopted despite the opposition of parliament's right-wing groups, was designed to shame the Council of Ministers and the Commission into acting on a proposal to end discrimination which the Commission produced three years ago.
"It is an opportunity for the EU as an employer to show the way, to be a good example," rapporteur Malou Lindholm told Reuters.

The Swedish Green Euro-MP cited the case of a homosexual Swedish Commission official, working in Brussels, whose partner had been prevented from living in Belgium, even though the gay couple were deemed to be married under Swedish law.
Not speaking French, the partner had been able to get a job in Brussels and the Belgian authorities had refused to let him stay in the country, she explained.
As for the upper age limit of 35, this discriminated against women who decided to have children and then retrain before returning to work, she said.

Lindholm said the Council, Commission and parliament should adopt the progressive stance taken by countries like Sweden and Denmark, international bodies like the United Nations and European Monetary Institute and companies such as the computer giant IBM.
She pointed out that the EU institutions' statutes dated back to 1958.
"Can you imagine any organisation or any company that in 40 years has not changed its statutes? The world has changed but the statutes have stayed the same," she complained.
Lindhom said Christian Democrat and Europe of Nations members of the civil liberties committee, which initiated the report, had tried to sabotage the initiative.
"Some only recognise a 'family' as consisting of one man, one woman and two children," she said.
The Swedish Euro-MP said she was encouraged by the positive attitude expressed on Wednesday by Erkki Liikanen, the commissioner responsible for staff matters.
But she recognised the most important task would be to convince the Council, which must take the final decision.
